newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia calls off Alcan talks.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia calls off Alcan talks.

text.p: The British Columbia government is abandoning negotiations with Alcan Aluminium Ltd over compensation for its cancelled Kemano hydroelectric project after the company filed a court action on the dispute, local media reported on Thursday.

Alcan said on Thursday it still wanted to pursue negotiations and was only filing the court case to protect its legal right to sue later if talks collapsed. The government and company have unsuccessfully negotiated for almost two years since the province in 1995 axed the half-built project, on which Alcan had spent C$535 million.
Local newspapers today quoted British Columbia Premier Glen Clark as saying that the province would not negotiate with Alcan as long as its lawsuit was pending.
"You can litigate or you can negotiate and we're prepared to negotiate, but if they pursue litigation we'll see them in court," he was quoted as saying.
Clark said the government could legislate a settlement to the dispute if necessary but that its case was so strong it should not have to do that.
"It's our position we're not on the hook one penny...we did them a favor by cancelling that project and that's the position we will take in court," Clark said, reported the Vancouver Sun.
